title: Proteomic Response to Copper-Induced Stress and Recovery in the Colonial Tunicate Botryllus schlosseri
projectDescription: The study investigated the proteomic response of the colonial tunicate Botryllus schlosseri to acute copper exposure and subsequent recovery. DIA analysis was performed on Botryllus schlosseri colonies exposed to copper concentrations of 0 µg/L (control, C0), 300 µg/L (C3), and 900 µg/L (C4) for 24 hours (Exposure phase, E). To assess recovery (R), a subset of colonies from each condition was transferred to clean seawater for an additional 24 hours. Each condition included 11 biological replicates, collected by pooling ≥15 zooids per sample (including vascular network and ampullae).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Samples were flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen post-treatment and stored at −80°C until processing. Protein extraction was performed using chemical and mechanical lysis in urea buffer with zirconium beads. Proteins were precipitated with cold acetone/TCA, reduced (DTT), alkylated (IAA), and digested with Trypsin/Lys-C. Peptides were desalted with C18 columns, dried, and resuspended in 0.1% formic acid. 100 ng  of Peptides were analyzed using a Bruker nanoElute® 2 system coupled to a Bruker timsTOF in DIA mode. Chromatographic separation used a C18 column (Aurora) with a 50-minute gradient from 3–33% acetonitrile.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw DIA data were converted to mzML using MSConvert. DIA-NN (v2.1.0) was used for precursor identification and quantification with a predicted spectral library from the B. schlosseri proteome (De Thier et al., 2025). Trypsin was set as the enzyme (2 missed cleavages), with carbamidomethylation (C) as a fixed modification, and oxidation (M) and acetylation (N-term) as variable modifications.
